hook_text: Turn over any plastic tub. That little triangle with a number decides whether it gets a second life or a hole in the ground.
clip_script: Plastics are a family, not one material, and they do not mix when melted. So they must be sorted, and the code tells you how. 1 PET: clear cooldrink bottles. 2 HDPE: milk bottles. 5 PP: margarine tubs and caps. Those three are worth money in South Africa and waste pickers collect them by the kilo. 4 is soft bags, some value if clean. 3 PVC, 6 polystyrene, 7 everything else: keep them out of the bag. Rinse it, cap off, check the code, sort, squash, bag. One PVC bottle ruins a batch of PET. A black tray fools the sorting machines. A crisp packet is 7, however shiny.
visual_style: Whiteboard triangle codes 1 to 7 with an item under each; three highlighted as valuable; a sorting table with piles; a bottle with its cap flying off; a black tray with a question mark.
mood: Brisk and useful, like a quick training at a depot.
pacing: Family, sort, seven codes, three that matter, method, traps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort twelve containers from your kitchen by code tonight.
